newsitem.title: USA: US LPG slump continues as many traders leave town.
newsitem.headline: US LPG slump continues as many traders leave town.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were mostly unchanged in thin trading Friday.
By midday, most deals heard done were in the Conway, Kansas, market. Propane there was done at 34.38 and 34.88 cents a gallon. September propane was heard done slightly higher at 35.25 cents.
Conway butane was done at 39.50 cents, and natural gasoline was done at 45.25 cents. Natural gasoline was pegged about a half cent higher than Thursday at 45.00/45.50 cents.

Traders said the only deal heard done in the Mont Belvieu, Texas, market was a 25,000-barrel parcel of propane at 35.50 cents. September propane values were pegged at 35.75/36.00 cents, a quarter cent higher than August values there.
Butane buyers in Belvieu were said to be looking for Enterprise barrels at 41.75 cents. Butane sellers there were asking 42.00 cents.
"It's extremely quiet. It's so thin that it's hard to know where the numbers are at," one Belvieu trader said. He said many traders were at an industry retreat in Lake Tahoe.
